name: Householder QR factorization
definition: For each trailing column x, choose α=−sign₊(x₁)‖x‖₂, v=x−αe₁ and apply H=I−2vvᵀ/(vᵀv) to the trailing block, skipping x=0. Accumulate Q in reflector order so A=QR.
variables: x trailing subvector, e₁ first unit vector, sign₊(0)=1, R upper trapezoidal, Q orthogonal
assumptions: Real m×n matrix, m≥n for the stated tall-design application
limitations: Triangular regression solve requires full column rank
failure_conditions: Triangular regression solve requires full column rank

source.citation: Anderson et al., LAPACK Users’ Guide, 3rd ed., QR Factorization. https://www.netlib.org/lapack/lug/node40.html

name: Column-pivoted QR for rank diagnosis
definition: At step k pivot the remaining column with largest trailing 2-norm into position k, then eliminate the trailing entries with a Householder reflector to obtain AP=QR. Estimate rank by thresholding the leading triangular block at a declared scale.
variables: A design, P column permutation, Q orthogonal, R upper trapezoidal, k pivot step
assumptions: Use a declared numerical rank tolerance and consistent feature units
limitations: Greedy pivoting does not guarantee strong rank revelation for every matrix
failure_conditions: Greedy pivoting does not guarantee strong rank revelation for every matrix
computation: O(mn²) for a dense tall design

source.citation: Anderson et al., LAPACK Users’ Guide, 3rd ed., QR Factorization with Column Pivoting. https://www.netlib.org/lapack/lug/node42.html

name: Complete orthogonal minimum-norm solve
definition: Given AP=Q[R₁₁ R₁₂;0 0] with rank r, use a right orthogonal factor Z such that [R₁₁ R₁₂]=[T 0]Z. Set x=P Zᵀ[T⁻¹(Qᵀb)₁:r;0], or x=0 at rank zero.
variables: A design, b response, Q and Z orthogonal, T nonsingular r×r upper triangular, P pivot permutation
assumptions: Rank known or resolved reliably and dense real design
limitations: A noisy near-null direction can change the solution substantially when the declared rank changes
failure_conditions: A noisy near-null direction can change the solution substantially when the declared rank changes
computation: Pivoted QR followed by right orthogonal transformations and a triangular solve

source.citation: Anderson et al., LAPACK Users’ Guide, 3rd ed., Complete Orthogonal Factorization. https://www.netlib.org/lapack/lug/node43.html

name: Partial-pivoting LU solve
definition: At each elimination step swap in a remaining row maximizing absolute pivot-column entry, then update the Schur complement using the resulting multipliers. Solve Ly=Pb and Ux=y from PA=LU.
variables: A square system, b right-hand side, P row permutation, L unit lower and U upper triangular
assumptions: Nonsingular real square A and nonzero pivots
limitations: Large element growth can amplify roundoff
failure_conditions: Large element growth can amplify roundoff
computation: O(n³) factorization and O(n²) per dense solve

source.citation: Anderson et al., LAPACK Users’ Guide, 3rd ed., Factorizations for Solving Linear Equations. https://www.netlib.org/lapack/lug/node68.html

name: Cholesky triangular solve
definition: Factor A=LLᵀ with L lower triangular and positive diagonal, then solve Ly=b and Lᵀx=y by substitution.
variables: A Gram or precision matrix, L Cholesky factor, b right-hand side
limitations: Near singularity can defeat the factorization at working precision
failure_conditions: Near singularity can defeat the factorization at working precision
computation: O(n³) factorization and O(n²) per dense solve

name: Symmetric-indefinite block LDLᵀ solve
definition: Use symmetric row-and-column pivots with 1×1 or 2×2 pivot blocks to obtain PAPᵀ=LDLᵀ. Solve successively with L, block diagonal D and Lᵀ, and undo permutation P.
variables: A symmetric matrix, L unit lower triangular, D symmetric block diagonal, P permutation
assumptions: A nonsingular symmetric system with invertible selected pivot blocks
limitations: An unpivoted scalar scheme can fail even for the invertible matrix [0 1;1 0]
failure_conditions: An unpivoted scalar scheme can fail even for the invertible matrix [0 1;1 0]
computation: O(n³) dense factorization and O(n²) per solve

name: Rank-truncated SVD least squares
definition: Factor A=UΣVᵀ and set x_τ=Σ_(σ_i>τ) v_i(u_iᵀb)/σ_i for τ≥0. This is the minimum-norm solution for the truncated design.
variables: A design, b response, σ_i singular values, u_i and v_i singular vectors, τ rank threshold
assumptions: Declare a threshold in design units using training data only
limitations: Substantial signal in a discarded direction biases the fitted margin
failure_conditions: Substantial signal in a discarded direction biases the fitted margin

source.citation: Anderson et al., LAPACK Users’ Guide, 3rd ed., Singular Value Decomposition. https://www.netlib.org/lapack/lug/node53.html

name: Orthogonal symmetric tridiagonal reduction
definition: For k=1,…,n−2, choose a Householder reflector H fixing the first k coordinates and send the tail of column k to a multiple of its first unit vector. Replace A←HAHᵀ so the accumulated relation is T=QᵀA_original Q.
variables: H embedded reflector, Q ordered product, T tridiagonal
assumptions: Real symmetric input; a zero tail needs no reflector
limitations: A nonsymmetric matrix needs a different reduction
failure_conditions: A nonsymmetric matrix needs a different reduction

source.citation: Anderson et al., LAPACK Users’ Guide, 3rd ed., Symmetric Eigenproblems. https://www.netlib.org/lapack/lug/node48.html

name: Orthogonal upper Hessenberg reduction
definition: For k=1,…,n−2, use an embedded Householder reflector H_k to eliminate column-k entries below the first subdiagonal by similarity. The result H=QᵀA Q satisfies H_ij=0 for i>j+1.
variables: A real square matrix, Q orthogonal product, H upper Hessenberg
assumptions: Finite real matrix; skip a zero elimination tail
limitations: Nonnormal eigenvalues can remain sensitive after the reduction
failure_conditions: Nonnormal eigenvalues can remain sensitive after the reduction

source.citation: Anderson et al., LAPACK Users’ Guide, 3rd ed., Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors and Schur Factorization. https://www.netlib.org/lapack/lug/node50.html

name: Two-sided orthogonal bidiagonal reduction
definition: Alternate left column reflectors and right row reflectors on the trailing block to obtain B=U₁ᵀAV₁ with B upper bidiagonal in its first n rows. Then σ_i(A)=σ_i(B).
variables: A m×n matrix, B reduced matrix, U₁ and V₁ orthogonal factors, σ_i singular values
assumptions: Real m≥n case with zero tails skipped
limitations: Bidiagonal reduction still requires a separate singular-value solver
failure_conditions: Bidiagonal reduction still requires a separate singular-value solver

name: Cholesky reduction for symmetric-definite eigenproblems
definition: With B=LLᵀ form C=L⁻¹AL⁻ᵀ via triangular solves. Solve Cy=λy and recover z=L⁻ᵀy so Az=λBz and zᵀBz=yᵀy.
variables: A symmetric objective, B positive definite metric, L Cholesky factor, λ eigenvalue
assumptions: Real symmetric A and B with B strictly positive definite
limitations: Ill-conditioned B can amplify errors under the coordinate change
failure_conditions: Ill-conditioned B can amplify errors under the coordinate change

source.citation: Anderson et al., LAPACK Users’ Guide, 3rd ed., Generalized Symmetric Definite Eigenproblems. https://www.netlib.org/lapack/lug/node54.html

name: Generalized Schur decomposition
definition: Compute QᵀAZ=S and QᵀBZ=T with independent orthogonal Q,Z, S upper quasi-triangular and T upper triangular. Extract generalized eigenvalues blockwise from det(S_block−λT_block)=0, using homogeneous coordinates for infinite eigenvalues.
variables: A,B real square pencil, Q,Z orthogonal factors, S,T Schur pair, λ generalized eigenvalue
assumptions: Regular pencil, so the determinant polynomial is not identically zero
limitations: A nearly singular pencil can make finite and infinite eigenvalues numerically hard to distinguish
failure_conditions: A nearly singular pencil can make finite and infinite eigenvalues numerically hard to distinguish
computation: O(n³) typical dense reduction and QZ iteration

source.citation: Anderson et al., LAPACK Users’ Guide, 3rd ed., Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors and Generalized Schur Decomposition. https://www.netlib.org/lapack/lug/node56.html

name: Componentwise linear-solve backward error
definition: Given residual r=b−Ax̂, compute η=max_i abs(r_i)/(abs(A) abs(x̂)+abs(b))_i using 0/0=0. This is the minimum common componentwise relative perturbation bound on A and b that makes x̂ solve the perturbed system.
variables: A system matrix, b right-hand side, x̂ computed solution, absolute values entrywise
assumptions: Unstructured componentwise perturbations and residual measured with sufficient precision
limitations: A small backward error can coexist with large forward error for ill-conditioned A
failure_conditions: A small backward error can coexist with large forward error for ill-conditioned A
computation: O(nnz(A)+n) for a sparse square system

source.citation: Anderson et al., LAPACK Users’ Guide, 3rd ed., Further Details: Error Bounds for Linear Equation Solving. https://www.netlib.org/lapack/lug/node81.html
